pr.title: Add project worktree, which prints the worktree that has a branch or a pull request's branch checked out
pr.head: 72abae652ec21e61ca07cee6af1e79e39cacce1f

summary: A Git worktree is a second working folder attached to the same repository, with its own branch checked out. Agents and review tools create many of them, and their folders are often named for an agent's id rather than for the branch, so the branch name alone does not tell you where a pull request's code lives on disk. Finding it meant reading git worktree list by eye.

This pull request adds project worktree <branch-or-number>. Given a branch, it prints the folder of the worktree that has that branch checked out. Given a number, it reads that pull request from the repository origin names and looks up its head branch the same way. It exits 66 and names the branch when no worktree has it.

The command only reads: it runs git worktree list and, for a number, one gh api request. It changes no branch, folder, or file. Because it is read-only, it joins the Codex allow rules that project init writes.

cards.title: What the command matches
cards.html:
• Whole names only. fix does not match fix/login.
  • Every worktree. The main checkout and every linked worktree, from inside any of them.
  • Not a detached worktree. A review's scratch worktree has no branch, so it never matches.
  • Not a folder Git marks prunable. Git marks a worktree prunable when its folder is gone, unless the worktree is locked.
  • All digits means a pull request. An argument of only digits is read as a pull request number, as project ios reads it.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The first head's CI failed because the new tests committed without a Git identity. The second head gives them one, and CI's check passes.
  • One open finding: a locked worktree whose folder was deleted still prints its missing path. Claude Code locks the agent worktrees it creates.

groups.title: Finding the worktree
groups.kicker: The command, and the helper that reads Git's worktree list
intro: run_worktree in cli.py turns the argument into a branch name, then asks worktree_on_branch in review.py for the folder. A number goes through review.read_pull_request, the call project review uses, and the pull request's head.ref becomes the branch.

worktree_on_branch reads git worktree list --porcelain -z. That output lists one record per worktree, with NUL bytes between fields and an extra NUL between records, so a folder name with a space or a newline comes through whole. The helper returns the first record with an exact branch refs/heads/<name> field and no prunable field.

checks.text: A pull request from a fork whose head branch has the same name as one of your branches, such as main, finds your branch's worktree. The pull request body names this limit, and docs/cli.md does not.

files.note: Adds worktree_on_branch, which parses the porcelain worktree list.

checks.text: Git never marks a locked worktree prunable, so a locked worktree whose folder was deleted still matches, and the command prints a missing path with exit 0. Claude Code locks each agent worktree it creates. A temporary repository with a locked, deleted worktree reproduces it. The fix the review asks for is to skip a record whose folder is not a directory.
git worktree list -z needs Git 2.36 or later. An older Git fails with an unknown-switch error.

files.note: Adds the worktree subcommand, run_worktree, and NoWorktree, which exits 66 as the other not-found errors do.

checks.text: Run by hand in a temporary repository: a branch with a slash printed its worktree, a number with no origin refused and named the missing origin, and a run outside a repository exited 69.

files.note: Builds a temporary repository with a nested branch name, a folder with a space, a detached worktree, and a deleted one, and fakes only the GitHub call.

checks.text: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m tests tests.test_worktree tests.test_permissions passed, 21 tests, and CI's check passed on this head.

groups.title: Allowing the command in Codex
groups.kicker: The Codex rules and the documentation
intro: project init writes a Codex rules file that lets Codex run read-only project commands without asking. This pull request adds worktree to that list, because the command changes nothing. docs/cli.md shows the same rules and gets a new section, "Find a branch's worktree".

files.note: Adds worktree to CODEX_ALLOW and to the reason Codex shows for the rule.
Adds project worktree with a number and with a branch to the table of commands each host allows.
Lists worktree in the documented Codex rules and adds the section that describes the command.

checks.text: test_the_documented_codex_rules_are_the_ones_init_writes compares the documented rules with CODEX_ALLOW, and it passed.
